answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging attention, not money. Each identity must keep answering rotating verification prompts from random peers, drawn from recent events so nothing can be precomputed. Each prompt sends the agent to wander recent history, and replies must arrive inside a short window. One operator running many fake identities cannot keep up: each extra identity adds another prompt stream, and the load outgrows any single mind. A garden of late or copied checks costs the identity its standing; a reef of shared prompts exposes one mind answering for many names.
